input.value: charred kitchen cabinets above stove, smoke damage on ceiling and walls

input.rationale: This is clearly property damage to the policyholder's own insured structure. The fire originated from the claimant's stove (an appliance within their home), causing direct physical damage to kitchen cabinets and smoke damage to ceilings and walls. This is a straightforward property damage claim covered under homeowners insurance.

The damage is localized to the kitchen area with charring on cabinets and smoke damage to walls and ceiling. While fire-related claims can be serious, the claimant was able to extinguish the fire quickly with an extinguisher, no injuries occurred, and damage appears contained to one room. Estimated damage likely falls in the $5,000–$25,000 range, suggesting a medium severity claim requiring standard processing and possible contractor assessment.

input.claim_summary: Homeowners policy POL-1001 (Alex Doe). Fire claim originating from grease flare-up on kitchen stove yesterday evening. Damage includes charred kitchen cabinets above stove and smoke damage on ceiling and walls. Fire was extinguished by claimant using fire extinguisher. No injuries. Damage contained to kitchen area. Deductible: $500; Coverage limit: $250,000. Severity: Medium. Estimated loss range: $5,000–$25,000. Requires contractor assessment and photographic documentation. No third-party liability exposure identified.
